tasks.title: At night our men and theirs are drawn the same
tasks.why: MEASURED, a controlled pair. Captures/night-1103/side0.png holds ten team-0 riflemen staged at 110,60; side1.png holds ten team-1 riflemen at the same coordinates with the same spacing, the first ten killed first (the world read back 'in box t0 0 t1 10'), the clock held at 120 and the camera identical (Shot(112,60,zoom 10,yaw 21), luma_mean 0.21773 in both, blown_frac 6e-05, pose_error_m 0). The two frames differ by at most 4 of 255 anywhere, and the bounding box of every pixel differing by more than 18 is None: changing the side of every man in frame changes nothing a player can see. By eye the crop at x 500-1100, y 300-700 of side1.png shows them as dark blue-grey shapes with a pale helmet rim, measuring hue 222 sat 0.48 against mud at hue 221 sat 0.53 - the same figure, the same colour, no ink line, no dot, no marker. This is not the figure-ground complaint of 2026-10-17 or 2026-10-19 (can you see a man at all): here a man is visible and still cannot be owned. It costs the player the first question he asks of a night field - is that knot of men mine or his - and he asks it exactly when he is deciding whether to send a trench over the top. decisions.md 2026-10-07 (d-frogs) already carries the owner's direction for sides: 'your side in blue and the enemy in red'. GUESS: a team tint is written for the day palette and lost in the night pass.
tasks.done_when: The pair reshot exactly as above (ten team-0 men staged at 110,60, clock held, Shot(112,60,10,21); those ten killed, ten team-1 men at the same spot, the same camera): the PIL bounding box of pixels differing by more than 18 between the two frames covers at least 2% of the frame (today it is None, max difference 4 of 255), and the brightest quartile of a crop on a man differs between the two frames by at least 20 degrees of hue, while blown_frac stays under 0.02 and luma_mean within 0.02 of today's 0.21773.

tasks.title: Lamp light turns pink and violet as it leaves the lamp
tasks.why: MEASURED, four frames of the same held scene plus a fifth. Close, the pools are the amber they are meant to be: on Captures/night-1103/tmclose_z8.png the brightest cells read hue 29-31, sat 0.89-0.93, val 0.83-0.89, and tmclose_z11.png carries 142 warm cells (hue 15-50, sat > 0.3) of 2283 lit. Pull back on the same focus and the warm goes: tm_z30.png has 36 warm cells of 1620 lit and tm_z16.png has 3 of 2271, while magenta cells (hue 250-345, sat > 0.12) number 50, 81, 42 and 30 across the ladder - brightest hue 344 sat 0.26 val 0.50 at (560,224) in tm_z30, hue 342 sat 0.26 val 0.46 at (1344,256) in tm_z60. It is not a scan artefact: on side1.png the same pool's skirt at x 520-620, y 300-360 measures rgb 0.517 0.405 0.406, hue 359, sat 0.22, and its core at x 500-560, y 300-330 hue 307, sat 0.08 - a salmon-pink ring round a violet-grey middle, plainly pink to the eye in tm_z16.png at x 200-460, y 280-360 (hue 287, sat 0.17). decisions.md 2026-09-29 is flat: 'Every light is warm; blue is only moonlight and its reflections... No stray blue or purple sparkles'. It costs the one rule the night teaches a player - warm means fire, lamp, danger - because at the distances he plays at, lamp light is neither warm nor moonlight but a third colour. GUESS: the pool colour is laid under the fog and distance pass rather than through it.
tasks.done_when: The same ladder reshot on one lamp cluster with the clock held (Shot at zoom 8, 16, 30 and 60): in a 16 px cell scan of each frame, every cell with value over 0.35 and saturation over 0.12 sits in hue 15-50 or in the moonlight blues (hue 190-250) - today 81 cells at zoom 16, 42 at zoom 30 and 30 at zoom 60 sit in hue 250-345 - and the count of warm cells (hue 15-50, sat > 0.3) at zoom 16 is at least a quarter of the zoom-8 frame's (today 3 against 142), with luma_mean within 0.02 of today's 0.22205 so the night has not been lifted.

tasks.title: A machine alight close up blows out the frame
tasks.why: ONE-VIEW, so MINOR. Captures/night-1103/burn_z14.json reads blown_frac 0.02442 with the warning 'more than 2% of the frame is blown out' on a machine set alight (VfxLab.Burning(4,92,100)), shot with the clock running at zoom 14; the same machine at zoom 24 a moment later (burn_z24.json) is fine at blown_frac 0.00364, luma_p95 0.36163. So the burning hull is past the rig's own INVALID bar at the close band, where a player goes to watch a kill, and the flame tops out as flat white instead of the cel flame tongues the look asks for. It is NOT the star shell wash of 2026-10-17 (that is the whole field, from a flare) and not the machine's ground band of 2026-10-19 (hue, not level): the burning machine otherwise reads well, clearly hotter than the healthy machine beside it, with a warm ground pool. One frame only: a second Shot at zoom 14 on a different machine set alight, clock running, would settle whether it is this hull or every burning machine.
tasks.done_when: Two machines set alight with VfxLab.Burning and each shot with the clock running at zoom 14: blown_frac is under 0.02 in both sidecars (today burn_z14.json reads 0.02442) while luma_p95 stays above 0.5, so the fire is still the brightest thing in the frame.
